alignments.note: Substantival article nominalizing the quoted phrase; the ASV supplies determiner plus generic noun *this word*. Rule 102 gives both words to the article and heads the unit on the supplied noun *word*; rule 60's closing clause keeps the head on the nominal rather than on the demonstrative determiner. No participle follows, so rule 32 is not in question.

ἅπαξ → *once*, with *more* as a rule 7 helper completing the English idiom *once more*. Reading *more* as a discontinuous second word of ἔτι (*Yet … more*) is defensible; I kept it with ἅπαξ because *once more* is the single English adverbial phrase the numeral adverb licenses.
Anarthrous Greek noun with a supplied *the*; rule 51's anarthrous clause makes the determiner an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun it determines.

Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronominal expression and nothing else, so *those things* is the article's and the relativizer and copula stay with the participle. The genitive case preposition *of* rides along under rule 21, and rule 22 heads the unit on the nominal word *things*.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; *that* and *are* are rule 7 and 9 helpers on the participle under rules 31 and 32, headed on the lexical verb.

Anarthrous substantival participle; no article competes, so the supplied *things*, the relativizer *that*, the auxiliaries and the case preposition *of* are all rule 7 and 9 helpers on the participle, headed on the lexical verb *made* under rules 9 and 17.
Purpose ἵνα realized by the word introducing its English clause, rule 40.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it only the pronominal expression *those things*, the relativizer staying with the participle; headed on the nominal word under rule 22.
Ordinary negative μή with the participle → *not*. Rules 41 and 59 do not apply: the following word is a participle, not a negative indefinite.
Participle rendered as a finite relative clause; *which* and *are* are helpers on it under rules 31 and 32, discontinuous around the negative under rule 15, headed on the lexical verb.
Subjunctive with its modal auxiliary; rule 9 heads the unit on the lexical verb *remain*.

review_notes: Variant SBLGNT.HEB.12.27.v018 is underdetermined and its base fallback is compatible with the ASV; no textual decision taken inside the alignment file (rule 12), and the unit carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark, so rule 97 is not in question.
Both σαλευομέν- units and both governing articles are analysed alike (rule 24): article keeps the pronominal expression, participle keeps the relativizer and copula.
All 15 source and all 31 target ids are partitioned exactly once; no unrepresented or added units were needed.
